correctness.rationale: Factivity and full introspection are exactly equivalent to a partition into accessibility classes, one full-support downset per class. Inclusion-exclusion counts those families, and the standard exponential formula counts all labelled frames. The exact exceptional first partition contributes n*c_(n-1). The proof bounds every other partition by central-binomial convexity plus Kleitman–Markowsky growth of Dedekind numbers, giving a vanishing ratio to n*c_(n-1); it also proves c_n/M(n)→1 and n*c_(n-1)/c_n→0. The included standalone checker independently enumerates all 1–3-world semantic maps and confirms small arithmetic cases. Finite checks are not used as a proof of the asymptotics.

originality.rationale: The new target is the sharp probabilistic concentration and first rare-partition profile for the full labelled one-agent inquisitive epistemic frame class. Existing structural semantics, the block counts (A006126), the exponential labelled-set construction, and the Dedekind estimate are expressly credited and not presented as novel. Inspected source articles, relevant published-finding corpus records, database checks and dedicated term/sequence searches did not supply or dominate the conditional probability limit. A more general uninspected superexponential assembly theorem could nevertheless subsume it; absolute historical originality is not claimed.
residual_risks: An older or unindexed equivalent enumerative treatment of labelled inquisitive epistemic frames may exist.
A strong generic theorem on superexponentially weighted labelled assemblies could imply the conditional asymptotic, although none was found in the inspected evidence.
The complete older long-form Ciardelli–Otto paper was not read page-by-page; its accessible formal and concluding sections were checked.
The numerical antichain-cover sequence itself is classical and must not be characterized as newly discovered.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete labelled frame count coupled to a sharp probabilistic typical-structure law, not a routine small-case table. It determines the quantitatively dominant failure mode of global epistemic indistinguishability and demonstrates that rich inquiry-state choices force a single epistemic cell with probability tending to one. Such conditional exceptional structure is not obtainable from a small-census computation or from the known block weights alone without substantial asymptotic control. It clarifies a finite-model semantic class used to interpret questions and knowing-wh.
